correctness.rationale: Pointed one-move profiles are classified: empty matching has only equal/up; maximal matching has equal/down/incomparable for n>=3; nonempty nonmaximal matchings for n>=4 have all four relation categories. Every non-maximal X has at least two unmatched vertices, with exactly binomial(n-2|X|,2) strict single-edge extensions; but the number of ALL strict upper matchings is one precisely when exactly two vertices are unmatched, since with >=3 vertices at least three distinct upper edge extensions exist. n-2|X|=2 can occur only for even n, realized by matching of size (n-2)/2. Independent combinatorial checks across n=2..11 corroborate boundary. The EF rank-two type recurrence establishes optimality for parity, though the theorem does not claim complete rank-three theories.
